title: Ex 3.3 #9 · Length-6 lists with two vowels side by side
prompt: Make lists of length 6 from the letters A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, with no letter used twice. How many of these lists have two vowels in consecutive positions? (The only vowels here are A and E.)
answer_format: A whole number, or an expression for it like 26^4 or binom(10, 3).

mistakes.hint: That counts the lists with the vowel pair in one particular place, such as the first two positions. The pair can start in any of five places.
Once you've chosen where the two vowels go, they can appear as AE or as EA.
That counts every list of length 6, whether or not its vowels are side by side.

hints: There are only two vowels, A and E, so both must appear, next to each other.
Choose where the vowel pair starts, then its order, then fill the other four positions with distinct consonants.
solution: The vowels are A and E, so the list must contain both, in adjacent positions, and its other four entries are consonants.

The pair can occupy positions 1–2, 2–3, 3–4, 4–5 or 5–6 (5 choices) and can read AE or EA (2 choices). The other four positions take distinct consonants from the six available: $6 \cdot 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 = 360$ ways.

reference.note: This exact exercise, restated in ProofLab's words. Uses the multiplication and addition principles (Sections 3.2 and 3.3).
